subject: General Awareness
summary: The making and features of the Indian Constitution, the most-asked articles, schedules and amendments, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Fundamental Duties, the Union executive and Parliament, the judiciary and constitutional bodies, and Panchayati Raj and municipalities (with Delhi's special status). DSSSB regularly asks 'which article deals with...' and article/schedule pair questions, so the article map is the core of this note.

sections.heading: Making and salient features of the Constitution
sections.body:
The **Constituent Assembly** first met on **9 December 1946**; **Dr Rajendra Prasad** was its president and **Dr B.R. Ambedkar** chaired the **Drafting Committee**. The Constitution was **adopted on 26 November 1949** (now Constitution Day) and came into force on **26 January 1950** (Republic Day). As adopted it had **395 articles, 22 parts and 8 schedules**; today it has **12 schedules** and many more articles (inserted as 21A, 243A and so on).

The Preamble declares India a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic**; 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)**.

**Borrowed features** (frequently asked):
- UK: parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, bicameralism.
- USA: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independent judiciary, impeachment of the President.
- Ireland: Directive Principles, nomination to Rajya Sabha, method of electing the President.
- Canada: federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre.
- Australia: Concurrent List, joint sitting.
- Germany (Weimar): suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency.
- USSR: Fundamental Duties. South Africa: amendment procedure. France: liberty, equality, fraternity, republic.

sections.heading: Article map: the articles asked most
sections.body: Learn articles in blocks rather than as isolated numbers: Part III (12-35) is Fundamental Rights, Part IV (36-51) is DPSP, 51A is duties, 52-151 the Union, 152-237 the States, Part IX (243-243O) Panchayats, Part IXA (243P-243ZG) Municipalities, 245-263 Centre-State relations, 264-300A finance and property, 352-360 emergency, 368 amendment.

sections.heading: Schedules and landmark amendments
sections.body: Memory aid for the schedules: 1 territory, 2 salaries, 3 oaths, 4 Rajya Sabha seats, 5 and 6 tribal areas, 7 lists, 8 languages, 9 protected laws, 10 anti-defection, 11 panchayats, 12 municipalities. The 8th Schedule began with 14 languages and now has **22** (Sindhi added by the 21st Amdt; Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali by the 71st; Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali by the 92nd).

sections.heading: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Fundamental Duties
sections.body:
There are **six Fundamental Rights** (Part III):
- Right to Equality (Art 14-18): equality before law (14), no discrimination (15), equal opportunity in public employment (16), abolition of untouchability (17), abolition of titles (18).
- Right to Freedom (Art 19-22): six freedoms of Art 19, protection in respect of conviction (20), life and personal liberty (21), education (21A), safeguards against arrest (22).
- Right against Exploitation (Art 23-24): no trafficking or forced labour; no child below 14 in factories or hazardous work.
- Right to Freedom of Religion (Art 25-28).
- Cultural and Educational Rights (Art 29-30).
- Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32), called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Ambedkar.

The Right to Property was removed from Part III by the **44th Amendment** and is now a legal right under **Art 300A**. The five **writs** are habeas corpus (produce the detained body), mandamus (perform a public duty), prohibition (stop a lower court), certiorari (quash an order of a lower court) and quo warranto (by what authority one holds an office). The Supreme Court issues them under Art 32 and High Courts under Art 226, which is wider because it also covers ordinary legal rights.

**DPSP** (Art 36-51) are not enforceable in courts but are fundamental in governance; examples: village panchayats (40), uniform civil code (44), early childhood care (45), environment protection (48A), separation of judiciary from executive (50).

**Fundamental Duties** (Art 51A) were added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the **Swaran Singh Committee**'s recommendation; there were 10 originally and the **11th** (parents to provide education to children aged 6-14) came with the **86th Amendment (2002)**.

sections.heading: President, Vice-President and Parliament
sections.body:
**President** (Art 52): elected indirectly by an electoral college of the **elected** members of both Houses of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi and Puducherry). Minimum age 35; term 5 years; removed by **impeachment (Art 61)** for violation of the Constitution, needing a two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House. Powers include pardons (Art 72), ordinances when Parliament is not in session (Art 123) and emergencies (Art 352, 356, 360).

**Vice-President** (Art 63): elected by all members of both Houses (nominated members included); is ex officio **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (Art 64) and acts as President in a vacancy (Art 65).

**Prime Minister and Council of Ministers** (Art 74-75): aid and advise the President and are collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**.

**Parliament** = President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha (Art 79).
- **Lok Sabha**: directly elected, 5-year term, minimum age 25; presided over by the Speaker.
- **Rajya Sabha**: a permanent House; maximum 250 members, of whom **12 are nominated** by the President for literature, science, art and social service; one-third retire every two years; members serve six years; minimum age 30.
- A **Money Bill** (Art 110) can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha; the Speaker certifies it; the Rajya Sabha can only delay it for 14 days.
- A **joint sitting** (Art 108) is presided over by the Speaker and is not available for Money Bills or constitutional amendments.

sections.heading: Judiciary and constitutional bodies
sections.body:
The **Supreme Court** (Art 124) began functioning on 28 January 1950. Parliament fixes the number of judges by law. Judges retire at **65** (High Court judges at **62**) and can be removed only by an order of the President after an address passed by a special majority in each House on proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Jurisdiction: original (Centre-State disputes, Art 131), writ (Art 32), appellate, advisory (Art 143), and it is a court of record (Art 129).

**Constitutional bodies** are created by the Constitution itself; **statutory bodies** by an Act of Parliament; **executive bodies** by a government resolution.

sections.heading: Panchayati Raj, municipalities and Delhi
sections.body:
The **Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957)** recommended a three-tier Panchayati Raj; **Rajasthan (Nagaur district) was first, on 2 October 1959**.

**73rd Amendment (1992)**, in force from **24 April 1993** (National Panchayati Raj Day):
- Part IX, **Art 243-243O**; Eleventh Schedule with **29** subjects.
- **Gram Sabha** (Art 243A); three tiers - village, intermediate, district (the intermediate tier may be skipped by States with population below 20 lakh).
- Fixed term of **five years (Art 243E)**; fresh elections within six months of a dissolution.
- At least **one-third** of seats and chairperson posts reserved for women; reservation for SCs/STs in proportion to population.
- **State Finance Commission** every five years (Art 243I) and **State Election Commission** (Art 243K).

**74th Amendment (1992)**: Part IXA, **Art 243P-243ZG**; Twelfth Schedule with **18** subjects; three kinds of bodies - **Nagar Panchayat** (area in transition from rural to urban), **Municipal Council** (smaller urban area), **Municipal Corporation** (larger urban area); District Planning Committee (243ZD) and Metropolitan Planning Committee (243ZE).

The **PESA Act 1996** extends Panchayat provisions to Fifth Schedule areas.

**Delhi**: the **69th Amendment (1991)** inserted **Art 239AA**, making Delhi the National Capital Territory with a Legislative Assembly and a Council of Ministers; public order, police and land remain outside the Assembly's legislative power. The Lieutenant Governor is the administrator.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Which pair is correct? I. Article 239 - Administration of Union Territories II. Article 241 - High Courts for Union Territories
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Part VIII (Art 239-242) deals with Union Territories. Art 239 provides that UTs are administered by the President through an administrator. I is correct.
Step 2: Art 241 lets Parliament constitute a High Court for a UT or declare an existing court to be its High Court. II is correct.
Answer: **Both I and II**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Under which article can the Vice-President act as President when the office falls vacant? (A) 52 (B) 61 (C) 65 (D) 72
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Eliminate by meaning: 52 creates the office of President, 61 is impeachment, 72 is pardoning power.
Step 2: Art 63-65 deal with the Vice-President; Art 65 makes him act as President during a vacancy or absence.
Answer: **(C) Article 65**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Which statement is correct? I. Fundamental Duties were part of the original Constitution of 1950. II. The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Amendment.
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Fundamental Duties (Art 51A) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, so they were not in the original text. I is wrong.
Step 2: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Art 21A and the 11th duty on parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6-14. II is correct.
Answer: **Only II**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Identify the type of body: Finance Commission, NITI Aayog, National Human Rights Commission.
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Ask where each body comes from.
Step 2: Finance Commission - named in Art 280, so **constitutional**.
Step 3: NHRC - created by the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993, so **statutory**.
Step 4: NITI Aayog - created by a Union Cabinet resolution (2015), so **executive** (neither constitutional nor statutory).

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Which article deals with the duration of Panchayats, and what is the term?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Part IX runs 243 to 243O; 243A is Gram Sabha, 243B constitution of panchayats, 243D reservation.
Step 2: Art **243E** fixes the duration: **five years** from the first meeting, with elections before expiry or within six months of a dissolution.
(Compare: Art 172 for State Legislatures and Art 83 for Parliament.)

pitfalls: Confusing Art 32 (Supreme Court writs, a Fundamental Right) with Art 226 (High Court writs, wider scope).
Writing Art 21 for education; education is 21A, life and personal liberty is 21.
Thinking the President is elected by all MPs and MLAs; only elected members vote (nominated members do vote in the Vice-President's election).
Believing a Money Bill can start in the Rajya Sabha; it is introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Saying Fundamental Duties came with the original Constitution; they were added in 1976.
Calling NITI Aayog a constitutional body; it is an executive body.
Assuming the right to property is still a Fundamental Right; it is a legal right under Art 300A.
Mixing the 11th Schedule (Panchayats, 29 subjects) with the 12th (Municipalities, 18 subjects).
quickRevision: Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949, in force 26 Jan 1950.
Original Constitution: 395 articles, 22 parts, 8 schedules; now 12 schedules.
42nd Amendment 1976: Socialist, Secular, Integrity; Fundamental Duties.
44th Amendment 1978: property removed from Fundamental Rights (now Art 300A).
Art 21 life and personal liberty; Art 21A education 6-14.
Art 32 heart and soul of the Constitution (Ambedkar).
Art 44 uniform civil code; Art 51A Fundamental Duties.
Art 61 impeachment; Art 72 pardon; Art 123 ordinance.
Art 148 CAG; Art 280 Finance Commission; Art 315 PSCs; Art 324 Election Commission.
Art 343 Hindi in Devanagari is the official language of the Union.
73rd Amdt: Part IX, Art 243-243O, 11th Schedule, 29 subjects; 74th Amdt: Part IXA, 12th Schedule, 18 subjects.
Art 239AA (69th Amdt, 1991): Delhi as National Capital Territory with an Assembly.
Rajya Sabha: 12 nominated members; Lok Sabha min. age 25, Rajya Sabha 30, President 35.
